messages:
morgan: PTAL — I pushed a follow-up to PR #1287 that addresses the review comments and adds a short smoke test. I'm planning to run canary tomorrow morning; question on process: should I squash the fixups now or wait and squash only after the canary passes? happy to do whichever the team prefers. cc @alejandro @sam

alejandro: skimmed the diff, looks clean. smoke test entrypoint? :+1:

morgan: smoke command is:
```
./scripts/run_smoke.sh --pr 1287 --env canary
```
It just runs the small kv-allocator e2e and a basic latency check.

ci-bot: smoke job queued for commit 9f3c8b2 — build started.

sam: tiny nit in test name but non-blocking. If we wait to squash, we keep history for debugging which I prefer. :thumbsup:

sasha: I agree with sam — keep commits until canary is green. Ops: any objections about canary window?

ops-bot: Canary capacity available: 2025-07-09 06:00-08:00 UTC. No other rollouts scheduled in that slot.

morgan: perfect, I'll schedule canary for that window. I'll also add a note in the PR description with the canary time and what to watch for (latency reg, allocation errors).

alejandro: PTAL approved — thanks for addressing the comments, morgan. Will watch the canary.

sam: approved.

sasha: approved.

ci-bot: smoke job passed on commit 9f3c8b2 (all checks green).

morgan: awesome — I'll proceed with the canary. If it passes, I'll squash into a single PR commit and queue for merge during the window. If it fails, I'll keep the branch and file a follow-up. Thanks everyone! :seedling:
